stories.headline: Michael Carrick set to lead Man United vs. Bournemouth amid pressure - sources
stories.summary: Michael Carrick is set to be in charge of Manchester United against Bournemouth this weekend, sources have told ESPN, as he battles to keep his job at Old Trafford.
stories.body:
Michael Carrick is set to be in charge of Manchester United against Bournemouth this weekend, sources have told ESPN, as he battles to keep his job at Old Trafford.

Carrick is under mounting pressure following the disastrous 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Despite serious concerns internally about the team's form, the 45-year-old is expected to be on the touchline when United face Marco Rose's side on Sunday.

Having only signed a two-year contract in May, Carrick's long-term future remains in doubt after a run of seven games without a win and just one Premier League victory all season.

The club's hierarchy accept that if results do not turn around quickly they will be forced into a change, but there is also sympathy for Carrick's predicament.

Senior staff were left shocked at the team's performance against Como and felt that only Amad Diallo, who was introduced as a half-time substitute, emerged with any credit.

Sources have also told ESPN that there is a feeling that too many players are refusing to take personal responsibility for their own role in the team's slump.

Bruno Fernandes was substituted in the 67th minute at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium before appearing to criticise Carrick and his staff for their tactics in a post-match interview.

- Michael Carrick hits back at Bruno Fernandes criticism after Man United loss

- Man United's worst league starts ever: How does 2026-27 compare?

- Frank Leboeuf blasts Bruno Fernandes for 'betrayal'

The United captain is the second senior player to turn his fire on club staff in as many weeks after Lisandro Martínez directly criticised director of football Jason Wilcox and the board following the 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid.

Martínez later issued a public apology and received a fine. Sources have told ESPN that Fernandes' comments will be assessed before a decision is made about whether to take any further action.

Carrick is set to hold his usual weekly news conference on Friday afternoon to preview Bournemouth's visit to Old Trafford.

United's first-team squad will report back for training on Friday after being given a day off on Thursday, sources have told ESPN.

Information from ESPN's Mark Ogden was used in this report.

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: Previews, stats and betting intel for Thursday's dozen games
stories.summary: Get your multi-view ready, hockey fans, it's another busy night!
stories.body:
Regular readers of NHL Tonight know that with it being Thursday there will be a lot of hockey games tonight.

Indeed, with a dozen contests, it's yet another night where it pays to have Power Play on ESPN+, along with a heavy dose of the multi-view option.

Here's a look at what you need to know for each of tonight's 12 contests, including betting info and broadcast details:

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Nashville Predators at Boston Bruins

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | BOS -155, O/U: 5.5

There's another new format for the All-Star Game this season -- a round-robin, 3-on-3 tournament with teams composed of players based on nationality. Various players skating in this game could be on the ice in February for that event, including American Olympians Jeremy Swayman and Charlie McAvoy, with Czechia native David Pastrnak joining Team Rest of World.

Is there a case for Steven Stamkos to make Team Canada? The future Hall of Famer has 10 points through eight games, after netting 42 goals last season.

New York Rangers at Toronto Maple Leafs

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NYR -112, O/U: 6.5

If the season was over right now, these are two playoff teams! There are more than 70 games remaining on each team's calendar so let's not draw up the parade routes just yet, but it's notable for the fact that neither was close to a playoff berth in 2025-26.

The Rangers have been the beneficiary of a breakout performance by Dylan Garand, while the Leafs have been paced (unsurprisingly) by Auston Matthews and William Nylander, along with newcomer Kirill Marchenko and 21-year-old Easton Cowan. Who earns the valuable two points out of this one?

San Jose Sharks at Ottawa Senators

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | OTT -130, O/U: 6.5

Two of the biggest trades this summer included the Senators: the trade sending Brady Tkachuk to Florida, and the subsequent deal to land Sharks winger William Eklund (using the No. 9 pick from the Panthers in that swap). The Sens were reunited with Brady on Wednesday, but the Sharks will not get to see their old pal William on the ice on Thursday -- he's out several more weeks after ankle surgery.

Nevertheless, the healthy Senators will hope to slow down a potent Sharks attack that knocked off the Canadiens earlier this week.

Anaheim Ducks at New Jersey Devils

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NJ -198, O/U: 6.5

To some degree, both of these teams were expected to be in the playoff picture by season's end. To do that, they'll both need to start stringing wins together. The Ducks went oh-fer on their other stops in the NYC metro area, extending their current losing streak to four games.

The Devils have had some impressive wins lately (4-3 over the Avs, 7-1 against the Rangers), but have also been on the wrong side of lopsided losses to the Sens, Mammoth and Islanders.

Florida Panthers at Pittsburgh Penguins

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | FLA -105, O/U: 6.5

If nothing else, Penguins games have been exciting this season. Pittsburgh is scoring 3.30 goals per game, and allowing 3.80; that's fun for everyone! Florida will be playing this game 24 hours after the emotional high of taking on Brady Tkachuk's former teammates in Ottawa. Can they summon a second wind against Sidney Crosby & Co.?

Los Angeles Kings at New York Islanders

7:30 p.m. ET (Disney+/ESPN+/Hulu) | NYI -120, O/U: 5.5

It took seven games, but the Kings are finally on the board with a victory in 2026-27! The defiant 5-2 win was emblematic of what they haven't done much of this season: scoring goals (with just 12 total in the six prior games).

That newfound offense will be put to the test against one of the game's finest netminders, Ilya Sorokin, who is fourth this season in both goals-against average (1.72) and save percentage (.934).

Vegas Golden Knights at St. Louis Blues

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | VGK -120, O/U: 6.5

Speaking of scoring, the Golden Knights have two players on the Top-10 scoring leaderboard at this juncture -- Jack Eichel and Mark Stone -- both of whom are on pace to finish with career highs in points.

Standing in their way is Blues goalie Joel Hofer, who got back on track with a 32-save win against Winnipeg on Tuesday following a five-goals-against loss to the Wild.

Winnipeg Jets at Dallas Stars

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DAL -205, O/U: 5.5

Prior to the trade request/holdout/suspension of Connor Hellebuyck, this game had shaped up to be a showdown between two of the top American goalies of this generation, with Jake Oettinger manning the crease for the Stars.

Regardless, there are still two very important points on the line for both the Stars -- who come in on a three-game heater -- and the Jets -- who have lost three straight after a better-than-expected start.

Minnesota Wild at Calgary Flames

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MIN -192, O/U: 5.5

On paper, this one doesn't look too close. But on some nights, the Flames look like they can play with -- and beat -- just about anyone. To wit, their recent wins over the Hurricanes and Ducks.

Or, it could turn out like losses to Colorado (7-3) or Vegas (6-2).

Carolina Hurricanes at Edmonton Oilers

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CAR -115, O/U: 6.5

A potential Stanley Cup Final preview? This matchup has a 2.51% chance of occurring, per Stathletes projections. And while those who like "big markets" might prefer them to be on the biggest stage, there is no shortage of star power in this matchup.

Edmonton's Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard -- along with Carolina's Sebastian Aho -- are all among the top point scorers this season.

Utah Mammoth at Seattle Kraken

10 p.m. ET (Disney+/ESPN+/Hulu) | UTA -162, O/U: 6.5

It might be surprising for some to see the Mammoth atop the mighty Central Division standings after 10 games, although their inspired postseason appearance was a clue that something big is being built in Utah.

But the Kraken's hold on the No. 3 spot in the Pacific? That qualifies as a legitimate shock, given what the franchise had done in recent seasons. This contest will be an important one for both teams to continue building their identity as legit contenders in the West.

Detroit Red Wings at Vancouver Canucks

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DET -170, O/U: 6.5

After winning two of their first three games this season, the Canucks have regressed back to essentially where many believed they'd be, and lost their next eight.

The Red Wings are trending in the opposite direction, with at least one point in each of their past five (two wins, and three OT/SO losses). Do both trends continue on Thursday?

stories.summary: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 7, led by alternate looks from Houston, Detroit and Dallas.
stories.body:
The throwbacks were well-represented in Week 6 of the NFL slate. While that's still the case this week, it's the alternates that lead the way -- including two monochromatic looks from the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions.

Houston will be wearing its "battle red" combination, which the team first unveiled in 2024. It's all red from head to toe complete with a similarly colored matte lid that includes a new bullhorn logo. The numbers are deep steel blue with a liberty white trim, while the red pants boast blue and white stripes. The New York Giants will counter with all-white.

Also unveiled in 2024, the Lions are rocking their all-black threads against the Green Bay Packers. The black jersey and pants include a Honolulu Blue matte helmet with leaping Lions logo in silver. There's also a black stripe across the middle. Detroit first wore black uniforms in 1948 before bringing it back in 2005 as an alternate. The team stopped wearing them after the 2007 season before returning it in 2024.

The Dallas Cowboys will don their color rush look against the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football." Dallas unveiled these threads in 2015 with a silver helmet before an arctic white one debuted in 2022. The all-white combination has navy blue numbers and on the shoulder for a neat look.

Though alternates are the headliners, fans of the classics aren't leaving empty handed either in Week 7.

The Seattle Seahawks are wearing their throwbacks from the 1990s, complete with royal blue jerseys and silver pants and helmet. Seattle wore them last week on "Thursday Night Football." For the first time this season, the Atlanta Falcons and New York Jets are rocking classic uniforms. New York's is appropriately named "The Classic," and the all-white look pays homage to the 1968 championship season. It also includes uniform details from 1998 to 2018. Atlanta's threads include its iconic red helmet, which dates back to the 1960s, with black jerseys and white pants.

stories.headline: Rays die-hard Dick Vitale is ready for Tampa Bay's World Series spotlight
stories.summary: The famed ESPN broadcaster has a deep passion for Tampa Bay baseball, and he'll be in the stands for the Rays' World Series home games.
stories.body:
If the broadcast cameras pan to the stands above the visitors' dugout during Game 3 of the World Series at Tropicana Field on Monday, there's a decent chance they'll catch the Tampa Bay Rays' most vocal celebrity fan.

ESPN's Dick Vitale.

From a background standpoint, Vitale doesn't exactly cut the profile of your usual celebrity superfan. The New Jersey native -- born almost 60 years before the Rays played their inaugural season -- grew up a passionate fan of the local teams in the Tristate area and, as a baseball fanatic in particular, spent plenty of time at New York's assorted historic ballparks.

It makes for a remarkable list of all-time venues and players borne witness to: Yankee Stadium, the Polo Grounds, Ebbets Field. Mickey Mantle, Duke Snider, Willie Mays.

Vitale was partial to the Yankees and Mantle as a child. But eventually, as his professional career in coaching and then broadcasting evolved, he would settle in Florida. And when Tampa was awarded an expansion team by Major League Baseball in the 1990s, the legendary commentator was all-in. He quickly moved to grab season tickets ahead of the Rays' maiden campaign in 1998, and he has stuck with the club ever since.

"When I moved here, when I really moved here, I believed in being loyal with the Rays, the Bucs and the Lightning," Vitale told ESPN. "Loyalty is something that's important to me.

"It's just fantastic. There's some great baseball; we have great seats right by the visitors dugout. ... I love baseball, I've loved baseball for many, many a year, and I really enjoy going to the ballgames, getting a chance to meet some of the players, etc., and having a blast."

Make no mistake, Vitale's Rays love isn't just a local side quest, and the season tickets aren't just so he can catch a game now and then -- the fandom bona fides are real. He's happy to gush about Evan Longoria or Junior Caminero, and he can offer home run stats from the last two seasons for the latter off the top of his head.

Or, if you want another form of proof of just how locked in Vitale is, just check his social media during and after big games.

The Rays have played nine games this postseason. Every single one, win or lose -- and it's been mostly wins for Tampa Bay this postseason -- has gotten at least one post before, during or after the game.

The ever-active-on-X Vitale has posted about the Rays 32 times since the team's playoff run started. Monday's American League pennant-clinching win over the Cleveland Guardians alone prompted six.

Asked if he's got a prediction for Tampa Bay's upcoming World Series clash with the Milwaukee Brewers, Vitale gave an unsurprising answer. He was never going to go against his adopted home team.

"Well, you know I'm not going to go against them," Vitale said. "[I'm] reading the Brewers [are] totally favorites; I'm going Rays in seven, baby. And I will be there, all the home games, I will be at all of them."

stories.headline: UFC 333 preview and picks for featherweight, men's bantamweight titles
stories.summary: Check out the matchups and expert predictions for both championship fights at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi.
stories.body:
How does a fighter know when to stop when they're fighting well?

It's a question that, unfortunately, rarely gets answered in MMA. For every athlete who retires from the sport on their own terms, there are at least two athletes being retired by the sport. It is rare for a fighter to go out on a win, and infinitely rare for a fighter to go out on top.

UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski (28-4) is starting to look that question in the face. Volkanovski will look to defend his title at UFC 333 on Saturday against 32-year-old Movsar Evloev (20-0) in Abu Dhabi, UAE. Volkanovski, 38, already is defying the rules of Father Time. In April 2025, he became the first fighter older than 35 to win a UFC championship belt in a weight class under 170 pounds. He defended that title in January against 31-year-old Diego Lopes.

In the past, Volkanovski has been dismissive, even comedic, of his age, starring in self-deprecating "Old Man Volk" skits on the internet. Ahead of UFC 333, however, he's been discussing age far more seriously, saying that any fight moving forward could be his last.

"There's a reason this is not often done," Volkanovski told ESPN. "I will bring up [my age], because I think it adds to the story. A lot of people are thinking about it. The young, undefeated guy -- facing the old, 38-year-old."

Evloev, of Russia, is one of the most proven title challengers in featherweight division history, with a perfect 10-0 record inside the Octagon, but he hasn't finished a single UFC opponent. He is a slight underdog against Volkanovski, according to DraftKings -- a credit to how good Volkanovski has looked, as well as lingering doubts on Evloev's ceiling.

Volkanovski, a two-time champion who suffered back-to-back knockout losses to Islam Makhachev and Ilia Topuria before regaining his title in 2025, told ESPN he believes he will actually look better than ever on Saturday, due to Evloev's style. The undefeated challenger is known primarily as a position-focused grappler, who might struggle to match Volkanovski's striking and scrambling ability.

"His style is a perfect matchup for me, I truly believe that," Volkanovski said. "I'm not delusional, saying I'm the best I've ever been at age 38. I'm not in my prime. But stylistically, I think you guys will be saying, 'I swear this is the best Volk we've ever seen.'"

Even if that is the case, odds say Volkanovski is tempting fate with every performance from this point forward. Male UFC fighters 38 and older have won 37% of their bouts all time, according to ESPN Research. Volkanovski has acknowledged as much and even proposed a "sendoff" title fight against 37-year-old lightweight champion Justin Gaethje next, after which they would both retire.

Volkanovski has stated he's taking it one fight at a time, but he is talking about retirement now, which shows he understands the decision is in front of him.

"One hundred percent, if I notice I'm slowing down or I'm taking more damage, [I'll retire]," Volkanovski said. "I said that before my last fight, too. A lot of people look at me saying that and say, 'Look how he's talking, his head isn't in it.' I'm just real and I'm honest. I said it before my last fight, and what happened? I went out there and made it look easy."

More storylines to watch

Dvalishvili looks to prove the last fight was an outlier
Merab Dvalishvili attempted to make history at the end of 2025, when he fought Petr Yan in his fourth men's bantamweight title defense of the calendar year. The feat has never been accomplished -- or even attempted -- and it proved to be too much as Dvalishvili lost a five-round decision. He later revealed he went into the bout with a significant knee injury and had a terrible camp. Dvalishvili (21-5) will try to recapture his title against Yan (20-5) in the UFC 333 co-main event.

Although he's admitted to tough circumstances around their last meeting, Dvalishvili has also said he doesn't regret pursuing UFC history and won't use those circumstances as an excuse, crediting Yan for the victory.

But the fighters' shared history has obviously raised the stakes for this Saturday. Dvalishvili and Yan have met twice, with Dvalishvili dominating their first meeting in March 2023. If Yan wins the trilogy, against a much fresher version of Dvalishvili than he saw in December, it could push Dvalishvili toward the back of the line for another title shot.

Not the last chance, but kind of the last chance
Not to put unnecessary pressure onto Aaron Pico's shoulders, but the truth is that any type of loss to Losene Keita -- a promising talent who is only 1-1 in the UFC -- would have heavy, long-lasting implications.

Pico, 30, has won 10 of his past 12 fights, but this is still a crossroads. He's been viewed as championship material since before his professional MMA debut, but has endured violent, memorable setbacks at various points in his career, including a spinning back elbow knockout loss to Lerone Murphy in his UFC debut 14 months ago. There is still massive potential in Pico, and he had an impressive bounce-back win against Patricio Pitbull in April, but he's in a risky position this weekend. He faces a dangerous but relatively unknown opponent in Keita after his original opponent, Arnold Allen, was forced off the card. Saturday's outcome will go a long way in determining how matchmakers and fans view him moving forward.

Coaches' questions and predictions for the title fights

Can Evloev significantly control Volkanovski on the ground?
Evloev is good everywhere, but Volkanovski has such an ability to game plan and show up in the big moments. Evloev is super big and strong. He has good standup, great transitions and ground control. But Volkanovski was able to get up after being taken down by Islam Makhachev. Are we just gonna forget that? Islam is now a welterweight. Volkanovski is so intelligent and so good at finding ways to exploit guys. His fight IQ is as good as anyone I've ever watched. He showed it against Lopes in their rematch in January. If Evloev cannot control Volk on the ground for long periods of time, Volkanovski will win a decision. And with the modern emphasis on damage when it comes to scoring, judges don't want to see you unsuccessfully try to hold someone down. Volkanovski by decision. -- Sayif Saud, Fortis MMA

Will age catch up to Volkanovski?
The biggest X factor is that unknown: At what point does Volkanovski's age slow him down? He's fighting one of the purest wrestlers/grapplers in the UFC in Evloev. I could see Evloev trying to prove he can stand with Volkanovski at times and win over the UFC, but I don't think that would be his smartest decision. Personally, I believe that "Old Man Volk" still has it. He's proven time and again he's going to win those key wrestling scrambles, and I believe he'll end up catching Movsar. It will be a grinder of a fight, but Volkanovski's experience being in there with bigger, stronger guys like Islam will pay off. Volkanovski by TKO. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

Can Dvavishvili hurt Yan with his hands?
We know that Yan has the physicality to compete with Merab's wrestling. He didn't avoid the takedown in their last fight -- he actually got more takedowns than Merab. That's a fact. And Yan on the feet is so dangerous, you have to give his standup the edge. If he comes in in great shape and can counter-wrestle and have the same physicality he did in December, he can win. The biggest technical question is whether Merab can create enough offense to get inside and hurt Yan with his hands. If the wrestling gets shut down, can he create offense? If Merab can hurt Yan on the feet, that changes the whole fight and throws it in favor of Merab. I've got Yan winning by a slight edge. -- Saud

Who will control the resets?
Yan needs to control the range, punish Merab's entries and continually invest in the body. He needs to establish the center and force Merab to initiate his wrestling from a distance, and intersect those entries with straight punches, body shots and uppercuts. I'd like to see him keep that lead arm frame, to establish his underhooks right away with his wrestling defense. He doesn't need to eliminate the takedown attempt, but he does need to make Merab pay for every failed attempt. Merab, meanwhile, has to weaponize pace, create chaos and disrupt Yan's comfort. He has to chain together multiple takedown attempts, so that even failed attempts affect Yan's rhythm. Who will control the resets? Merab thrives when one attack becomes three or four; Yan thrives when he's able to reset and return to technical striking. I lean Yan by decision again. --Eric Nicksick, Xtreme Couture

stories.headline: Christian Horner to Mercedes? Ex-Red Bull boss reveals pre-Toto Wolff approach
stories.summary: Christian Horner has revealed he rejected an offer to become Mercedes' Formula 1 team principal in 2012, before the team appointed his future rival Toto Wolff.
stories.body:
Christian Horner has revealed he rejected an offer to become Mercedes' Formula 1 team principal in 2012, before the team appointed his future rival Toto Wolff.

Horner claims in his new autobiography, Drive, that F1 legend and Mercedes' new non-executive chairman Niki Lauda -- with whom he had previously discussed Lewis Hamilton's future -- visited his home during the off-season and offered him a substantial salary to leave Red Bull.

The former Red Bull boss says he turned down the opportunity out of loyalty to the team he had helped build, with Mercedes subsequently embarking on a period of dominance under Wolff and Hamilton.

"Maybe our interactions over Lewis had stuck with him because later that year, during the Christmas break, Niki came to my house and asked me to join Mercedes as his team principal," Horner wrote.

"I was caught off guard. Leaving Red Bull had never crossed my mind. When he then laid out a series of dazzling numbers, I realized he was discussing my potential salary.

"'Red Bull will never pay you what Mercedes can,' he said. 'I respect you as a racer. I want you to come. Besides, Helmut [Marko, Red Bull adviser] is a miserable b------.'"

The approach came after Horner had held discussions with Lauda about Hamilton's future, with the British driver considering leaving McLaren at the end of the 2012 season. Hamilton held ultimately unfruitful talks with Red Bull due to the finances involved, but Horner knew Lauda and Mercedes would be interested.

Indeed, Hamilton joined Mercedes for 2013, while Horner remained at Red Bull, where Vettel had just secured his third consecutive world championship.

"I listened to his offer and shook my head," Horner wrote. "At that point, Sebastian was at the peak of his powers and Red Bull were in the ascendancy.

"'Niki, I've been winning World Championships with Red Bull,' I said. 'I've built everything from scratch. I feel a loyalty to Dietrich and the team. So as much as I appreciate this, I'm not going to join Mercedes.'"

- Horner: Red Bull blocked moves for Leclerc and Alonso

- Rafael Câmara to Haas: How he could shake up Ferrari's future

- How Kimi Antonelli can win the F1 title at the US Grand Prix

Mercedes subsequently recruited Wolff from Williams in January 2013, with the Austrian going on to oversee one of the most successful periods in F1 history.

Mercedes won eight consecutive constructors' championships between 2014 and 2021, while Hamilton claimed six drivers' titles with the team.

Horner, meanwhile, remained at Red Bull until his dismissal in July 2025, overseeing four world championships with Vettel and another four with Max Verstappen.

Reflecting on Mercedes' decision to bring Hamilton and Wolff together, Horner admitted he initially underestimated the significance of the partnership.

"Their union was interesting but seemingly inconsequential," he wrote.

"In my mind, I was helping a friend while weakening McLaren, who were our closest rivals at that time. So, what was the worst that could happen?"

Drive, Christian Horner's autobiography, will be released on Oct. 22.

stories.headline: St. Louis City beats Columbus in Open Cup final for club's first trophy
stories.summary: St. Louis City won the first trophy in the club's history on Wednesday after defeating Columbus Crew on penalties to lift the U.S. Open Cup.
stories.body:
Backup goalkeeper Ben Lundt made a key save in the penalty shootout of a 120-minute 0-0 tie with the Columbus Crew to help St. Louis City SC win the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup on Wednesday night.

Timo Baumgartl gave St. Louis a 1-0 lead on the first penalty kick and then Lundt dove to his left to get a hand on Santiago Rodriguez's shot that deflected off the post.

St. Louis went 5 for 5 in the shootout, capped by Daniel Edelman's shot down the middle as goalkeeper Nicholas Hagen went the wrong way. Lukas MacNaughton, Chris Durkin and Damion Downs also scored.

St. Louis earned a spot in the 2027 CONCACF Champions Cup after securing the first major trophy in club history.

Columbus was seeking its second U.S. Open Cup title in club history.

Lundt entered the game in the 78th minute after starter Roman Bürki took a knee to the head while making a save. Bürki waved to the crowd while being carted off the field. Lundt came on in relief for his fourth appearance of the season.

It was the first U.S Open Cup final to go to penalties since 2015 when Sporting Kansas City beat the Philadelphia Union. The USOC is open to both professional and amateur clubs, but Major League Soccer teams have dominated the competition for more than two decades.

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return; Panthers lock in Patea
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news from the Dragons on some key outside backs
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Cowboys open to keeping Taumalolo

North Queensland are open to retaining Jason Taumalolo beyond 2027, with the veteran forward's assessment of how his body is holding up set to guide the next step.

ESPN understands the Cowboys will take their lead from Taumalolo as he weighs up his playing future, reflecting his standing as a club legend.

Taumalolo is contracted until the end of next season and becomes eligible to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 onwards from November 1.

Panthers lock in Patea
Penrith have secured Tua Patea until the end of 2029, with the youngster signing an extension that includes a pathway from a development contract into the club's top 30.

Patea capped off the 2026 season with a hat-trick in the Panthers' Jersey Flegg Grand Final victory, having started the year with an NRL training block.

The new deal will see him join Penrith's full-time NRL squad as he works towards a first-grade debut.

Bulldogs closing in on Skelton return

Jeral Skelton is closing in on a return to Canterbury following his departure from the Wests Tigers.

ESPN understands the Bulldogs are in advanced discussions to bring the outside back to the club for the 2027 season.

An agreement is understood to be close, although the deal has yet to be finalised.

Multiple NRL sides eye Knights forward

A Sydney club and a Queensland-based club are monitoring Newcastle forward Mat Croker ahead of November 1.

ESPN understands the two clubs have shown interest in the 27-year-old, who is approaching the final year of his Knights contract and can negotiate with rivals for 2028 onwards from next month.

Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu

Multiple clubs are monitoring St George Illawarra outside back Setu Tu, with the Dragons yet to begin talks over a contract extension.

Tu is contracted until the end of 2027 and is expected to test the open market from November 1, when rival clubs can negotiate a deal for 2028 and beyond.

The former Warriors outside back joined the Dragons on a development contract this season and is set to move into the club's top 30 squad in 2027.

His ability to cover multiple positions across the backline adds to his appeal as clubs assess their recruitment options.

Rivals monitor Patea as open market looms
Penrith young gun Luron Patea is expected to test the open market from November 1, with multiple clubs keeping tabs on the promising prop.

Patea is contracted until the end of 2027, but the Panthers are yet to begin talks over an extension, leaving rival clubs poised to explore a deal for 2028 and beyond.

Penrith have not granted Patea permission to negotiate with other clubs before November 1.

The Panthers junior made his NRL debut in 2024 and has shown promise during his first-grade opportunities, providing another emerging option in Penrith's forward pack.

He is among several Panthers players approaching the final year of their contracts, with veteran prop Moses Leota also unsigned beyond 2027.

Roosters eye Dockar-Clay reunion
The Roosters have shown interest in a potential return for Zach Dockar-Clay as they explore options to bolster their hooking and utility depth.

ESPN understands the 31-year-old has emerged as an option following his departure from Manly, with discussions remaining at an early stage.

Dockar-Clay spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Roosters before joining the Sea Eagles on a one-year deal for 2026.

Manly confirmed his departure last month after a season in which he claimed the club's NSW Cup best-and-fairest award.

Bostock brushes Dragons links

Dolphins star Jack Bostock has dismissed recent links between himself and the Dragons, admitting this isn't the first time he'd been floated for a club switch.

"I've been linked to a few a clubs," Bostock admitted.

"I don't know about [the Dragons links]."

He said that while he "obviously sees it in the media," his sole focus is the Kangaroos.

Sloan's Dragons stay still a possibility

Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United consider defensive clearout in summer
stories.summary: Manchester United are considering refreshing their back four, with three senior defender's contracts up at the end of the season. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Manchester United are considering refreshing their back four, with three senior defender's contracts up at the end of the season. Meanwhile, Arsenal want £55 million in any potential deal for striker Viktor Gyökeres.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, and Lisandro Martínez are playing for their futures at Old Trafford, with their contracts due to expire next summer. That's according to according to TEAMtalk, which claims that United are not rushing to make a decision on the three defenders. That comes as preparations are being put in place for potential defensive reinforcements in 2027, with center back and left back set to be the main areas of consideration.

- Chelsea are showing interest in a move for Brighton midfielder Yasin Ayari, claims TEAMtalk. The 23-year-old Sweden international is in talks with the Seagulls over a contract extension, with his deal expiring in the summer, though the club has the option to extend it by a further year. However, while there are hopes of sealing a long-term stay with the club, talks have stalled over an improved contract. That has brought Chelsea into the conversation, with the Blues eyeing another swoop on Brighton, while Turkish Super Lig side Galatasaray are also monitoring the situation.

- If Viktor Gyökeres does leave Arsenal in the next year, then the North London club has set a valuation of £55 million on a potential exit, reports Football Insider. That is the same amount as the initial fee the Gunners paid Sporting CP to land the striker last summer. However, after a slow start to the current campaign, the Sweden international continues to be linked with a possible move away. Clubs in Italy, Spain, and elsewhere in England are keeping track of the situation, should the 28-year-old become available.

- Arsenal are among a group of teams following a potential switch for Monza striker Gustavo Varela. That's according to Mundo Deportivo, which claims that the Gunners are joined by Napoli and the 21-year-old's former club, Benfica, in keeping track of his progress. Varela has scored eight goals in seven matches across all competitions for Monza, making an impressive start with his new club. While Benfica is keen on a return, there is no clause that could guarantee a move back to Portugal, though there is a clause that will allow for the club to match an offer accepted from another club. However, with Arsenal and Napoli in the mix, that prospect has been described as difficult.

- Liverpool are in no rush to engage in conversations with Alexis Mac Allister over a new contract, despite the player voicing his disappointment at the lack of an offer earlier this season. That's according to The Telegraph, which claims that the Reds are yet to open talks, as the Argentina international has entered the final two years of his deal at Anfield. The 27-year-old moved to Merseyside from Brighton for £35 million back in 2023, and has featured 161 times for Liverpool since then.

Other rumors
- Manchester United, Arsenal and Newcastle United have all been keeping track of AS Roma defender Wesley, with the 23-year-old Brazilian valued between €50 million and €60 million by the Serie A club. (TEAMtalk)

- Nine clubs are tracking a potential move for Eintracht Frankfurt youngster Niko Ilićević, including the likes of Liverpool, Manchester City, Chelsea and Tottenham from England, alongside Barcelona and Real Madrid in Europe. The attacking midfielder has been monitored heavily by several other clubs. (TEAMtalk)

- Manchester City, Chelsea, Newcastle United, Everton and Leeds United are the latest teams to be tracking Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi, 22, after attracting attention from plenty of teams with his Champions League displays. (Ekrem Konur)

- Barcelona and Atletico Madrid are among the sides monitoring the future of Lisandro Martínez, with the Manchester United defender now in the final year of his contract. United hold the option of an extra year on his deal. (Ekrem Konur)

- Liverpool are continuing to work on a new contract for Rio Ngumoha, with the club setting a clear stance on no exit for the 18-year-old winger in the coming transfer windows. (Fabrizio Romano)

- Lorenzo Lucca could leave Napoli in the January transfer window, with the 26-year-old striker free to move in the winter. (Nicolò Schira)

- Everton are eyeing a deal for Dinamo Zagreb striker Dion Beljo as one of several options for the forward ranks this January. The 24-year-old has 15 goals in 15 games for his club this season. (Football Insider)

- Gleison Bremer could push to leave Juventus in the January transfer window, with Bayer Leverkusen pushing to land the Brazilian defender. (La Gazzetta dello Sport)

stories.headline: Stanley Cup odds: Central-leading Mammoth see odds shorten after hot start
stories.summary: The Carolina Hurricanes are favorites to win the 2027 Stanley Cup while the Utah Mammoth rise.
stories.body:
Since their inaugural season in 2024-25, the Utah Mammoth have continued to gain momentum as a franchise and bookmakers took notice, assigning them the 14th-best Stanley Cup odds going into the 2026-27 campaign at 30-1. Now, after a strong start to the season that has them leading the Central Division at 7-3-0, the Mammoth are 19-1 for the Cup.

Because the Mammoth are not a naturally popular team, and Utah is not a state with legal betting, they haven't attracted as much attention as Caesars Sportsbook head of hockey Karry Shreeve thinks they should, though it's more than in previous seasons.

"Utah is finally starting to get a little bit more public traction," he told ESPN before the season. "Those odds aren't going to demand the same attention as some of those other teams would. So, I think like anything else ... there could be value on Utah as the season goes along for some of the future stuff anyways."

The reigning champion Carolina Hurricanes lead the pack of Stanley Cup contenders and have shortened from +650 to +600 since the start of the season. The Tampa Bay Lightning (10-1 to +800) and Washington Capitals (17-1 to 11-1) continue to improve with strong performances, while the Florida Panthers have lengthened from +650 to +850 since the start of the campaign after being one of the buzziest teams of the offseason.

stories.headline: WNBA's greatest 30 players: Snubs, underrated players and future greats
stories.summary: We ranked the top players of all time in the WNBA. Who got snubbed? Did Angel Reese or Caitlin Clark receive votes?
stories.body:
There is no such thing as a perfect ranking when it comes to determining the top players in any sport, but it is always an interesting exercise to try. That's what we did in selecting the WNBA's top 30 players as the league is winding down its 30th season.

Among the pitfalls of such rankings are so-called recency bias and the opposite of that, where perhaps current players don't get as much credit as historical stars. But our voting panel was made up of observers with different perspectives on the WNBA, which hopefully balanced the process.

Still, inevitably there will be questions about where players were ranked and who didn't make the list, as voted on by a panel of 23 ESPN reporters and staffers. Let's look at some of the biggest questions.

Who are the biggest snubs among retired players?

Let's start with three-time WNBA champion Penny Taylor. She is the only player on ESPN's all-time Top 25 list for the league's 25th anniversary in 2021 (she was No. 25 then) who did not make the top-30 ranking.

Taylor's stats are good enough (13 seasons, 13.0 PPG, 4.4 RPG, 3.0 APG), and the 6-foot-1 forward was a big factor in all three WNBA Finals the Phoenix Mercury won.

(By contrast, two players who were retired by 2021 but didn't make our Top 25 made the cut this time: forward Swin Cash and guard Deanna Nolan. Like Taylor, each won three league titles.)

Voters also strongly considered guard Ticha Penicheiro and forward Chamique Holdsclaw, who each appeared on six ballots.

Which current veterans were the hardest to leave off?

There are six active players in our top 30: Centers A'ja Wilson, Brittney Griner and Jonquel Jones, forwards Breanna Stewart and Alyssa Thomas, and guard Chelsea Gray. That doesn't count forward Nneka Ogwumike, who just retired from the WNBA at the end of this season.

Guard/forward DeWanna Bonner, who is playing with the Atlanta Dream in the WNBA Finals and finishing her 17th WNBA season, is the active player who came closest to making the list but just missed.

Other active players who got strong consideration from voters were guards Courtney Vandersloot of the Chicago Sky and Jackie Young of the Las Vegas Aces and Minnesota Lynx forward Napheesa Collier.

Which young players seem most likely to make a future list?
Guard Caitlin Clark and forward Angel Reese -- who is currently playing in the WNBA Finals, where she has led the Atlanta Dream to a 2-1 lead -- were the Nos. 1 and 7 picks in the 2024 WNBA draft and already have proved to be the top players in their draft class. Clark has averaged 20.2 points and 8.4 assists in her career, and Reese has averaged 15.0 points and 12.6 rebounds.

Both have played just three seasons, with Clark limited to 13 games during her second year in the league because of injuries. They will need more time to build their credentials, but from what we've seen so far, both project to be among the league's all-time best. Both received votes; Clark appeared on five of 23 ballots and Reese on four.

Guards Paige Bueckers and Olivia Miles, who followed Clark the past two seasons as respective Rookies of the Year, seem likely to be in this discussion someday as well.

Which players perhaps should have been higher?

With a group of players who are already in the Naismith Hall of Fame or will be in the future, the order of the top 10 is particularly difficult. Still, seeing Candace Parker at No. 9 will be jarring to some, considering the two-time MVP is undoubtedly one of the most talented players in WNBA history. Many might view Parker as a top-five player, and there is a good case for that.

However, five of the players ranked ahead of her also have won multiple MVPs. And the three single-MVP winners ahead of her have strong cases, too: Diana Taurasi is the league's career scoring leader; Maya Moore played in the WNBA Finals six times in her eight-season career (winning four); and Tamika Catchings is a five-time Defensive Player of the Year.

stories.summary: Como head coach Cesc Fàbregas said he regrets telling his players to ease off towards the end of their famous 4-1 win against misfiring Manchester United.
stories.body:
Como head coach Cesc Fàbregas said he regrets telling his players to ease off towards the end of their famous 4-1 win against misfiring Manchester United.

The Champions League upstarts heaped pressure on Red Devils boss Michael Carrick by swatting aside the three-time European champions with ease on Wednesday evening.

Nico Paz marked a sparkling man-of-the-match display with a brace at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, where Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramón also struck for the ever-improving Serie A side.

But Fàbregas' pride in the performance was tinged by disappointment at seeing United substitute Joshua Zirkzee score a stoppage-time consolation, admitting he turned his attention to Saturday's match against Sassuolo during the closing stages.

"I believe that tactically speaking the team played a rather good game," the former Arsenal and Chelsea star said.

"I regret maybe the last 10 minutes when I was the one telling the team to slow down the pace because there was another game and maybe with a 4-0 lead they could have managed something.

"I told Tasos Douvikas not to run anymore, to stay in the middle and maybe that is what I regret, because I'm the first one who always pushes the fight until the end. That goal hurt me."

stories.headline: Party like it's 1982? What baseball looked like during Brewers' last World Series
stories.summary: It's been a long, long wait for Milwaukee fans to see their team play again on baseball's biggest stage in October.
stories.body:
It's time for Milwaukee to party like it's 1982.

On Friday, for the first time in 44 years, the Milwaukee Brewers will play in the World Series. Back then, the club's search for its first-ever pennant didn't last too long -- the Brewers won the American League just 12 years after starting play in Milwaukee. (The Brewers moved to the National League in 1998.) But after a seven-game series loss to the St. Louis Cardinals, a drought in the quest to make it back to the sport's final stage ensued.

Milwaukee has emerged as one of Major League Baseball's most consistent organizations in recent years. The Brewers have won five of the last six National League Central titles, and haven't dipped below 85 wins in a full season since 2016. However, they weren't able to win out over the rest of the NL's best come postseason time.

Until this year.

The Brewers stormed through the National League's playoff bracket in dominant fashion, dispatching the San Diego Padres three games to one before sweeping the Los Angeles Dodgers, a fittingly impressive run for a team that boasted the best regular-season record in the majors.

As a result, World Series baseball is back on the Wisconsin shores of Lake Michigan for the first time in nearly four and a half decades. Unsurprisingly, things have changed quite a bit around baseball since the Brewers last played in the Fall Classic.

Here's a look at what baseball and the other major U.S. sports looked like back in 1982.

Yount, Thomas and more lead the way for 'Harvey's Wallbangers'
The 1982 edition of the Brewers came with a memorable nickname: Harvey's Wallbangers, a play off a popular cocktail referencing the name of Brewers manager Harvey Kuenn and the squad's power-hitting bona fides. Kuenn didn't become manager until midseason, taking over in an interim capacity after Buck Rodgers was dismissed with the team sitting at .500 two months into the season. Kuenn got the team into second gear, and Milwaukee would win the AL East on the season's final day.

The key ingredient in the Brewers' surge? Home runs. Milwaukee clobbered 216 that season, 30 more than the next closest team. Among the team's leaders were Gorman Thomas (39), Ben Oglivie (34) and Cecil Cooper (32), with a trio of future Hall of Famers right behind in Robin Yount (29), Ted Simmons (23) and Paul Molitor (19). 1982 was a particularly stellar year for Yount, who won two of his career MVP awards and led the league in hits and slugging percentage.

Other league leaders
While Yount took home the American League's Most Valuable Player honors, the National League's award went to Dale Murphy of the Atlanta Braves. Murphy clubbed 36 home runs, led the NL in runs batted in and added a Gold Glove in the field for good measure -- and he'd win the award again in 1983, becoming just the ninth player to win the award back to back.

On the mound, in the NL, 37-year-old Steve Carlton delivered the final of his four Cy Young-winning seasons, recording a major-league-best 23 wins and 286 strikeouts on a MLB-high 295⅔ total innings pitched. On the American League side, another Brewer came home with high honors, as Pete Vuckovich won the league's Cy Young, amassing an impressive 18-6 record.

Clubs and alignment younger fans may not recognize
Did the earlier reference to the Brewers being in the American League throw you off? Well, there's plenty more where that came from. Major League Baseball in 1982 did not exactly mirror the sport we see today. Instead of three divisions of five teams per league, it was two divisions of seven in the American League ... and two divisions of six in the National League. Alignment accordingly was wacky -- the Detroit Tigers were in the AL East with the Brewers for instance, while the 1982 National League West winner was ... the not-particularly-western Atlanta Braves.

The teams weren't a one-to-one match to the modern day, either. The California Angels won the AL West that season, pre-dating future name changes to the Anaheim Angels, Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim and Los Angeles Angels. Meanwhile in the NL East, the Montreal Expos were alive and well, with the club's eventual relocation to Washington, D.C., still decades away.

Around the rest of the sporting world
While the Cardinals took the 1982 World Series home to St. Louis, the rest of the 1982-83 sports calendar would belong to the northeast in other major American sports.

Washington would be the first northeastern city to grab a title in the ensuing months, as its dominant NFL squad steamrolled the league to a 12-1 record and a Super Bowl crown in January 1983. New York was next in May, with the New York Islanders powering their way to a Stanley Cup Final sweep of the Edmonton Oilers, before the title luck headed back down I-95 to Philadelphia for the NBA Finals just days later -- the 76ers swept the Los Angeles Lakers in that year's championship series.

Circuit of the Americas

The Circuit of the Americas first hosted the United States Grand Prix in 2012, to mark the end of a five year wait since the race at Indianapolis.

Mario Andretti, who won the world championship in 1978, opened the track and it has become a popular race among drivers and fans alike with plenty of overtaking action and drama.

COTA is a varied circuit with straights, esses through to sector two, and a series of hair-pins in sector three. The high-speed corners takes some inspiration from Silverstone and Hockenheim.

What happened last time out?
Verstappen edged out Norris to take an imperious pole position by 0.291 seconds.

The Red Bull driver dominated the race and posed as a serious threat to McLaren's Norris and Oscar Piastri in the drivers' championship.

Norris finished second and cut his lead to 14 points to Piastri in the standings, who finished fifth. Verstappen ended the weekend only 40 points behind Piastri with five races left of the season.

Who will win this year?

Antonelli will be as focused as ever to claim his ninth victory of the season with one hand already on the drivers' championship trophy.

However, Mercedes are still working on how to best optimise its current upgrade package. Last time out in Singapore, the team ran Russell on the older specification, while Antonelli had the upgraded package.

Red Bull were labelled by rivals as the "team to beat" for the remaining six races of the season. There seems to be no stopping Verstappen, who has won the U.S. Grand Prix four times.

Don't count out Hamilton who holds the record for six wins around COTA and will be looking to get his seventh podium for Ferrari this season.

stories.headline: St. Louis GK Bürki stretchered off after collision in Open Cup final
stories.summary: St. Louis goalkeeper Roman Bürki was taken to the hospital after taking a knock to the head during the U.S. Open Cup final against the Columbus Crew.
stories.body:
St. Louis City goalkeeper Roman Bürki was taken to the hospital after taking a knock to the head in a collision during his team's U.S. Open Cup final win over the Columbus Crew on Wednesday night.

In an attempt to make a save in the 70th minute, Bürki took a knee to the head from Crew winger Anass Zaroury. He remained on the ground to receive medical attention before being stretchered off the field.

Bürki was able to wave to supporters as he was taken away from the pitch. St. Louis confirmed to ESPN that Bürki was conscious and moving all extremities on his way to the hospital.

The score was tied 0-0 at the time of the injury, but St. Louis went on to win the game in a shootout after Burki's backup Ben Lundt made a save to help his team beat the Crew 5-3 on spot kicks.

The win earned St. Louis, which began play in MLS in 2023, its first trophy in club history.

St. Louis City captain Bürki had 43 touches and three crucial saves before the injury. He played an integral role in maintaining the 0-0 draw before being replaced by Lundt after the head injury.

Bürki, who joined St. Louis from Borussia Dortmund in 2022, stopped a corner kick from Brais Méndez that appeared to be goalbound and a flurry of other shots just before sustaining his injury.

Eleven minutes of injury time was added due to Bürki's injury, but neither team scored before the end of regulation despite Columbus outshooting St. Louis 16-3, so the game went to extra time and penalties.

stories.headline: Way-too-early AFL tiers: There's a clear flag favourite; 'silly season' winners and losers
stories.summary: Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL season is done and dusted, but that hasn't stopped ESPN's senior writer Jake Michaels from turning his attention to next year. Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers!

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Your new premiership favourite

1. HAWTHORN

Who knows if the Hawks would have been premiers this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's heroics late in that dramatic preliminary final at the MCG. There's certainly a real argument they would have gone all the way. This side, which is expertly coached by Sam Mitchell, just added Zach Merrett and Ben King to its best 23, two more experienced players desperate for flag success. There won't be many games the Hawks don't start favourite in next year. Even if this club's 2027 season over/under was set at preliminary final weekend, I'd still be taking the over.

Should be great, but there are some questions

2. BRISBANE

3. FREMANTLE

4. SYDNEY

The Lions just completed a remarkable three-peat and it certainly wouldn't have been outrageous for them to hold top spot here. But losing Lachie Neale and Chris Fagan -- arguably the two most important pieces of the club's modern-day dynasty -- cannot be underestimated. How do they fill those seismic gaps? The Dockers were the dominant team of the home and away season and if we played out the last four minutes of the Grand Final 100 times they probably win 99 of them. Instead, Fremantle has to spend all offseason dwelling on the greatest missed opportunity in club history. How do they respond in 2027? As for the Swans, who are always somewhere around the mark, nobody can really be sure what to expect after the Pullman Hotel saga. So many fascinating questions.

Silly season winners

5. GEELONG

6. WESTERN BULLDOGS

7. CARLTON

8. COLLINGWOOD

Each of these teams will be counting down the days until the 2027 season after drastically improving their lists during the trade and free agency window. The Cats landed the dynamic Toby Greene, significantly upgraded their ruck department with the singing of Rowan Marshall, and bolstered their defensive stocks with Jordan Ridley. The Bulldogs scored the biggest prize of all in Zak Butters, but they were also able to pry away Jordon Butts from the Crows, a much needed acquisition to what's been a shaky defence. The Blues will go into next season with Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield, and almost certainly father-son talent Cody Walker, while the Magpies added dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan.

Silly season losers

9. MELBOURNE

10. ADELAIDE

While a bunch of teams we'd expect to be in the fifth-to-10th range clearly improved their best 23, the Demons and Crows did nothing of the sort. Adelaide literally brought in nobody and will have to deal with the loss of key defender Jordon Butts, who departed as a free agent for the Bulldogs. Melbourne did sign several names, but do we think any of Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, and Bodie Ryan can be needle movers in 2027? But hey, these were two sides I was down on this year and both ultimately outperformed expectations. Perhaps they do have it all figured out...

It's now or never

11. GOLD COAST

12. NORTH MELBOURNE

13. ST KILDA

If not now, then when? The Suns rocketed to co-flag favouritism this time last year after signing Christian Petracca and Jamarra Ugle-Hagan. They ultimately won just nine games and finished 13th on the ladder. Disastrous. Damien Hardwick is under serious pressure to get more out of this list. Meanwhile, the Kangaroos haven't played finals in a decade, but there's some newfound optimism after the senior coaching appointment of highly regarded Jaymie Graham and the signing of Nick Blakey, the biggest name the club has attracted in a decade. The Saints also need to show something early in 2027 or Ross Lyon could be on his way out ... again! But the real worry is not doing enough to ensure star midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera signs on.

It's going to be another long year

14. PORT ADELAIDE

15. GWS

16. WEST COAST

17. RICHMOND

18. ESSENDON

Perhaps I'm being a tad harsh on Port, who were pretty competitive this year. But at the end of the day we're taking Zak Butters out of a side that won just seven games. The Giants lost four of their best players in Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs, and will be relying heavily on their younger talent next year. And then there's the Eagles, Tigers, and Bombers -- three teams that combined for just nine wins this year. We all expect these sides to be somewhere around the bottom of the ladder.
